chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar who said: Narrated to me a man from our companions from Al-Hakam ibn 'Uteyba who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and the house was full of its people when an old man came up leaning upon his staff until he paused at the door of the house. He said, 'Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' Then he was quiet. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'And upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' Then the old man turned his face toward the people of the house and said, 'Peace be upon you.' Then he was quiet until all the people answered him and returned his greetings.

Then he turned his face towards Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, bring me near to you, may Allah make me a ransom for you. By Allah, I love you and I love those who love you. And by Allah, I do not love you and those who love you for greed in the world. And by Allah, I hate your enemies and keep away from them. And by Allah, I do not hate them and keep away from them due to a dispute that was between me and them. And by Allah, I permit what you permit and prohibit what you prohibit, and I await your command. So is there hope for me, may Allah make me a ransom for you?'

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'Come near, come near,' until he seated him by his side. Then he said, 'O you old man, a man came to my father Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and asked him about something similar to what you asked me. So my father (peace be upon him) said to him: If you die, you will return to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and to Ali and Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn and Ali ibn Al-Husayn. Your heart will be delighted and your chest will cool and your eye will be pleased, and you will be welcomed by the Spirit and the Fragrance with the Honorable Scribes if your soul reaches here' — and he indicated by his hand to his throat — 'and if you live, you will see what Allah has kept for your eye to be pleased with, and you will be with us in the Highest Peak.' The old man said, 'What did you say, O Abu Ja'far?' So he repeated the words for him.

The old man said, 'Allah is Great! O Abu Ja'far, if I die, I will return to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and to Ali and Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn and Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). My eye will be pleased, my heart will be delighted, and my chest will cool, and I will be welcomed by the Spirit and the Fragrance with the Honorable Scribes if my soul reaches here. And if I live, I will see what Allah has kept for my eye to be pleased with, so I will be with you in the Highest Peak.'

Then the old man sobbed and wailed, 'Haa, haa, haa,' until he rolled upon the ground. And the people of the house sobbed and wailed for what they saw of the condition of the old man. And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) came and wiped his tears from the corners of his eyes with his finger and flicked them away. Then the old man raised his head and said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, give me your hand, may Allah make me a ransom for you.' So he gave him his hand. He kissed it and placed it upon his eyes and his cheek, then uncovered his abdomen and his chest. Then he stood up and said, 'Peace be upon you.'

And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) looked at the scruff of his neck as he was leaving. Then he turned his face towards the people and said, 'The one who would love to look at a man from the inhabitants of Paradise, let him look at this one.' Al-Hakam ibn 'Uteyba said, 'I had never seen mourners at all resembling that gathering.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (family of the Imam)
key_terms.الرَّوْحُ وَالرَّيْحَانُ: The Spirit and the Fragrance (welcoming signs in the grave/afterlife)
key_terms.السَّنَامُ الْأَعْلَى: The Highest Peak (a place of honor in Paradise)
key_terms.يَثْلَجُ قَلْبُكَ: Your heart will be delighted/cool (from joy)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the old man who visited Imam Al-Baqir (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia doctrine of *al-Wala'* (loyalty) and *al-Bara'* (disloyalty) as the essential criteria for salvation, illustrating how sincere love for the Ahl al-Bayt transcends mere ritual. The emotional climax, where the old man weeps and the Imam declares him a 'man of Paradise,' underscores the spiritual efficacy of *mawadda* (affection) in securing intercession and proximity to the Prophet. Scholarly tradition often cites this narrative to validate the concept of *Ruh al-Rihana* (the breeze of Paradise) as a tangible reward for the faithful in the intermediate realm (*Barzakh*).
